source.title: Spatial-Scheduling Strategy for Irregularly Shaped Blocks Under Disruption in Shipbuilding
source.data_availability: The publication says experimental data and simulation results are available from the corresponding author upon request.

repetition_interpretation: The paper reports each Case9_50_x was repeated 15 times under identical parameters and matched disruption scenarios. Table 6 values below are published aggregates, not raw runs.

metric_definitions_to_reconstruct.Aur: Average utilisation rate of initial blocks / planar storage yard utilisation as defined in the paper. Exact numerator and denominator must be reconstructed from source instance and yard/aisle geometry.
metric_definitions_to_reconstruct.Act_s: Reported algorithm computational time in seconds. Hardware, implementation and stopping protocol must be matched before treating runtime as directly comparable.
metric_definitions_to_reconstruct.Vt_min: Reported total vehicle travel time in minutes. Exact route/travel aggregation must be reconstructed from the source model.

methods.PA: Proposed hybrid ABC + adaptive large neighbourhood search (ALNS) + disruption-recovery algorithm

assumption_deltas_to_probe_separately: Outgoing blocks are treated as fully relocated when incoming blocks arrive.
Loading and unloading durations are neglected.
The ordering of blocks arriving concurrently is not considered.
Adequate numbers and types of vehicles are assumed.
The published scalarized objective uses 0.5 weight for yard utilization and 0.5 weight for vehicle scheduling time.
forbidden_inference: Do not compare this aggregate fixture directly with synthetic corpus metrics or claim a reproduction until original instance geometry, disruptions, objective denominators, algorithm settings, hardware, repetitions and raw outputs are reconstructed.
